summary.title: How to create your own simple 3D render engine in pure Java
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a small software 3D renderer in dependency-free Java, covering orthographic projection, matrix rotation, barycentric rasterization, z-buffering, and flat shading.
keywords: 3d math primer for graphics and game development
takeaways: Points can be rotated by multiplying them with 3x3 rotation matrices, and several rotations can be combined into one precomputed matrix.
Triangles are rasterized into pixels using barycentric coordinates, and a z-buffer keeps only the nearest pixel at each location.
Flat shading scales a triangle's color by the cosine between its surface normal (from a cross product) and the light direction.
A sRGB-aware shading function converts colors to linear space before applying shade, which avoids overly fast darkening.
The author recommends the book 3D Math Primer for Graphics and Game Development for deeper rendering math.
summary.summary: The article builds a small 3D viewer in pure Java with Swing, starting from a window with heading and pitch sliders and a tetrahedron defined by triangles and vertices. It then adds matrix-based rotation, orthographic projection, and per-pixel rasterization using barycentric coordinates. A z-buffer fixes draw-order problems, and flat shading uses normals and a directional light with an sRGB-aware shade function. A final bonus subdivides the tetrahedron into a sphere-like shape, and the full source is linked as about 220 lines with no dependencies.
